extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, patent examiners, patent practitioners, and policymakers interested in patent examination quality
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, metrics, and practices the USPTO uses to ensure and measure the quality and efficiency of patent examination (time allocation, examiner performance, OPQA review, training, tools, pilot program evaluation, and reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimal balance between time, quality, and cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The optimal balance between time, quality and cost is a well-documented challenge that ubiquitously faces the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO regularly reviews and makes necessary adjustments to strike this balance; UAIA 2024 fee study and other analyses inform tradeoffs among these factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalibrated examination time assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: An updated method of assigning examination time based on the application’s classification 'picture' and specific application attributes (including overall number of claims, length of the specification, and number of pages in any filed information disclosure statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented FY20 to address time limitations and application complexity; USPTO data show this recalibration supports adequate examination time and improved quality (reflected in FY20→FY23 improvements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner production achievement categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance categories for examiner annual production achievement: Outstanding (>110%), Commendable (103-109%), Fully Successful (95-102%), Marginal (88-94%), Unacceptable (<88%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to interpret production outcomes (e.g., in FY23 >45% reached >103% of goal while <6% were <88%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory compliance metrics (per statute and jointly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent quality metrics are measured as compliance with each of the four patentability statutes (35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, 112) and with all four statutes simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO publishes compliance rates for each statute individually because stakeholders found an overall composite to obscure key drivers; examples of FY20→FY23 improvements are provided for each statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPQA random review process and sample volume
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA generates statutory compliance metrics via randomized reviews of Office actions (volume ~12,000 random reviews per year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA randomizes Office actions mailed within the previous seven-day period, assigns reviewers by technology area, and validates metrics through internal audits, TC feedback/rebuttal, comparisons to TC reviews, and external perception surveys; OPQA is organizationally independent and has no incentives for noncompliance findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action compliance rule (any claim error = action noncompliant)
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating an Office action, if any single claim has an improper determination under any statute (e.g., an improper rejection was included or a proper rejection was omitted), then the entire Office action is identified as noncompliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If found noncompliant the finding is verified by an OPQA supervisor and sent to the relevant TC for consideration and any appropriate action; conversely, if all claims are treated correctly under every statute, the Office action is compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Appraisal Plan (PAP) quality and production weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner Performance Appraisal Plan aligns examiner and Agency goals with production and quality elements equally weighted at 30% each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAP emphasizes improved search and including best prior art early, offers exemplary activities reflecting best practices (search, clarity, compact prosecution), supports distinguishing performance levels, and has been used to take adverse actions (over 500 examiners faced adverse actions since FY21 for unacceptable quality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted, data-driven TC and Corps quality action plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality improvement efforts are targeted and data-driven at the Technology Center (TC) and Corps levels to limit negative effects on pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA data (via the Master Review Form) identify root-cause reasons (e.g., deficiencies in double patenting rejections) which inform TC-specific training; pre/post assessments for directed trainings (e.g., double patenting) showed measurable mastery improvements (11% example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Master Review Form (MRF) to identify root causes
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA’s Master Review Form collects a plethora of root-cause reasons that drive statutory compliance and quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focusing training on specific, actionable issues identified by the MRF (e.g., detailed mapping of claims to prior art) is more impactful than broad-topic training (e.g., anticipation/obviousness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive and continual examiner training
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO provides a comprehensive, continual training program (legal, procedural, technical) with multiple teaching modes (virtual and in-person classroom, one-on-one mentoring, instructor-led, computer-based) that grows in complexity as examiners gain experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training includes Patent Training Academy residency, on-the-job coaching, Instructor-Led and Computer-Based courses, Patent Examiner Technical Training Program (PETTP), Site Experience Education Program (SEE), Technical Training on Demand (TTOD) including a 21-course AI curriculum with Carnegie Mellon, and mandatory workshops (e.g., Clear and Concise Writing). Training needs are assessed via OPQA data and annual training needs surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training outcome measurement and rubric assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Training effectiveness is measured using assessments that apply rubrics (e.g., a 9-standard rubric rated 1–3 for a writing workshop).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: writing workshop participants showed 12% improvement from pre-video to editing exercise and 6% from editing exercise to post-assessment (18% overall), supporting mandatory adoption of successful training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernization and use of advanced search tools (including AI)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO leverages state-of-the-art electronic tools to assist examiners in efficiently identifying the most relevant prior art, including AI reverse image search for design patents and AI-based searching tools 'More Like This' and 'Similarity Search' in PE2E Search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced tools reduce searching time and increase likelihood of identifying best prior art earlier in examination; USPTO will monitor tool impacts to ensure examination time remains properly calibrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and transparency of quality data
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality achievements are publicly available: statutory compliance metrics, process measures, and stakeholder perception surveys are published on USPTO.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate metrics are published with detail (per statute and combined rates) and are validated; USPTO maintains that individual statutory compliance metrics are more informative to stakeholders than an overall composite score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation and scrutiny of quality review procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality achievement data is extensively validated throughout the fiscal year and OPQA review procedures are regularly scrutinized for data strength and process integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation methods include internal OPQA audits, TC feedback/rebuttal, comparisons to TC reviews, monitoring the consistency of OPQA reviewers, and sample error reporting to support confidence in metrics (Table 3 sampling errors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot/small-scale program design, assessment, and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO implements small-scale trial programs (expedited/prioritized examination) that track implementation and performance data and stakeholder participation to assess effectiveness before broader launch; each program is publicized at inception and memorialized on a landing page at USPTO.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO distinguishes these small-scale trials from larger pilot definitions (scalability may be inapplicable for temporary programs); participation and outcomes are tracked (Table 4) and programs are announced via email, Federal Register, press releases, and landing pages (Table 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based policymaking for initiative design
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiatives include clear goals and performance measures and data collection to support evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: training needs identified by OPQA and annual surveys led to a multi-part writing workshop with measurable outcomes; USPTO uses data-driven design and assessment for initiatives and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder perception surveys as a quality input
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO conducts semi-annual perception surveys of frequent-filing customers (~3,000 rotated respondents) to capture impressions of examination quality overall and by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perception trends (FY09 onward) are used alongside statutory compliance metrics to interpret quality; FY24 Q4 highlighted a 6:1 ratio of Good/Excellent to Poor/Very Poor responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution against using post-grant invalidation rates as proxies for examination quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent invalidation rates from courts and PTAB are not necessarily an accurate measure of patent examination quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons include selection bias of litigated patents toward commercially valuable innovations, availability of more extensive post-issuance prior art searches and new evidence in litigation/PTAB, and temporal changes in law/technology (OPQA study showing 93% of grounds relied on at least one reference not before the examiner). Thus post-grant outcomes reflect litigation drivers as well as differing processes and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal that every Office action be compliant with all patentability statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO’s stated goal is for every Office action to be compliant with all of the patentability statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO communicates compliance rates with each statute and the combined rate; OPQA evaluates Office actions to determine compliance against all statutes and pursues follow-up where noncompliance is found.
